description: CRIT-105's passThreshold contains a non-binary, undefined qualifier: 'A real article markdown file exists with real, cited content (not template text)'. Unlike REQ-5(e)'s explicit mechanical threshold ('an objective, computable threshold, not a subjective judgment', specs/behavioral-spec.md:35), CRIT-105 gives no computable definition of what counts as 'cited' (a URL? a named source? a quote?) or how many citations satisfy it. Two reviewers could reach opposite PASS/FAIL verdicts on the identical artifact. This is exactly the grade-inflation risk the contract-review dimension is meant to catch: a criterion worded as an aspiration ('real, cited content') rather than a concrete, reproducible check.

evidence.snippet: passThreshold: "A real article markdown file exists with real, cited content (not template text); a real note.com draft key/URL was created via note_mcp's create_draft (not injected/forced) ..."
